chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from 'Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and Fadalah from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Rifa'ah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that the two said:

"The Qarin (one who combines Hajj and 'Umrah) is constrained (to remain in the state of Ihram), and he has said: 'And I stipulated, so release me where you detained me.'" He said, "He sends his sacrificial animal." We said, "Does he perform Tamattu' next year?" He said, "No, but he enters (for Hajj) with the same type of Ihram from which he exited."

key_terms.اَلْقَارِنُ: One who combines Hajj and 'Umrah in a single Ihram
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ: Performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one exits and re-enters Ihram)
key_terms.يُحْصَرُ: Is constrained or prevented from exiting Ihram early

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Qiran regarding their sacrificial animal and subsequent 'Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific ruling for a Muhrim in Qiran who is detained (muhsar) before completing their rituals, emphasizing that they must send their Hady to the Haram and re-enter Hajj in the same state rather than performing Tamattu' the following year. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly view on the continuity of the Hajj obligation for Qiran pilgrims compared to the separate nature of Tamattu'. The ruling ensures that the pilgrim fulfills the original intent of their vow without altering the structural integrity of the combined pilgrimage.
